decisions.reason: As an updated version of an already well-accepted trommel screen, it sits squarely in the firm's established screening knowledge base, so by 2022 management would see little reason to withdraw it.

The mobile high-speed flail shredders remain closely related to the firm's core mobile recycling machinery and service capabilities, which supports continued learning and commercial refinement rather than exit.

The mobile high-speed grinder fits the firm's existing mobile processing competences, but the earlier withdrawal of a green-waste grinder variant suggests some residual portfolio risk, so the withdrawal probability is somewhat higher than for the most established lines.
The stationary electric fine shredder matches the firm's stationary shredding expertise and strategic move toward resource-saving solutions, making it a product the firm is likely to keep improving.
Stationary single-shaft pre-shredders are strongly aligned with the firm's long-standing shredding know-how and industrial customer base, so absorptive capacity considerations favor retention.
